answer: Let trust propagate from independently anchored accounts by a length-t random walk on the attestation graph, with voting weight proportional to walk mass. A Sybil set S with conductance φ(S)=w(∂S)/vol(S) has little boundary flow, so its aggregate vote, absent independent anchors, is bounded by the probability of crossing that cut within t steps—not by its internal attestations. Even a nebula of colluding nodes gains no signal beyond its sparse external links; basalt-hard trust requires genuine paths from anchors.
